CURRENT USER MESSAGE: Why can a phone show its GPS position without mobile data, yet fail to show a detailed map?
ASSISTANT:
answers.text: A phone can show its GPS position without mobile data because GPS (Global Positioning System) relies on satellite signals to determine location. This requires only the phone's GPS receiver and does not depend on internet or cellular connectivity. However, GPS alone typically provides only a general position (latitude, longitude) and may not display a detailed map because the map data is usually stored locally or accessed via mobile data (such as 4G/5G) or internet-based services. Without mobile data, the phone cannot retrieve or render map layers, such as roads, buildings, or landmarks, which are needed for detailed navigation. Therefore, while GPS location is accurate and available offline, detailed maps require additional data sources that are not available in the absence of mobile data. [1]
